name: MXFP4 native hardware support on CDNA4 (MI350X/MI355X)
workarounds: MXFP4 is only available on CDNA4 (MI350X/MI355X) - not on CDNA3
MXFP4 runs at the same throughput as MXFP6 (9.2 PFLOPS on MI350X, 10.1 PFLOPS on MI355X)
MXFP4 uses block-scaled representation with per-block scaling factors
notes: CDNA4 adds native hardware support for MXFP4 (Microscaling 4-bit floating point) at 9.2 PFLOPS on MI350X and 10.1 PFLOPS on MI355X. This is 2x the OCP-FP8 rate and equal to the MXFP6 rate. MXFP4 uses the OCP MX block-scaled format where each block of elements shares a scaling factor (typically 32 elements per block). The key inference advantage is memory bandwidth: 4-bit weights halve the memory traffic vs 8-bit, which is the primary bottleneck in decode. AMD's product page prints 'Peak Microscaling Four-bit Precision Matrix (MXFP4) Performance 10.1 PFLOPs' with NO sparsity variant - so 10.1 PFLOPS is the DENSE figure. This is distinct from CDNA3 which has no FP4 support at all. The practical use case is weight-only quantization for memory-bound decode workloads. AMD's vLLM blog shows GPT-OSS-120B running with FP4 quantized weights and BF16 computation on MI355X.
